articles.title_orig: Pope Leo celebrates open-air mass before 700,000 people in Paris
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo celebrates open-air mass before 700,000 people in Paris
articles.content_orig:
Crowds line Place de la Concorde on second day of pontiff’s first official papal visit to France in 18 years
Hundreds of thousands of people lined the Avenue des Champs-Élysées in ⁠Paris on Saturday to attend an open-air mass with Pope Leo, on the second day of his visit to France .
The Vatican estimated 700,000 people turned out for the outdoor mass with the 71-year-old American pope – about 100,000 more than the number of people who had registered to attend.
It took place at the Place de la Concorde, the site of bloody executions by guillotine during the French Revolution – when Louis XVI’s staunchly Catholic rule was overthrown – and now the centre of the secular republic.
The choice of the site, a symbol of the French republic to many, was criticised by supporters of France’s strict legislation separating church and state in public life.
But cheers rang out in the crowd as the pope thanked ‌God in his homily for the chance to ‌visit France on a whirlwind four-day, three-city tour to promote Catholicism and its teachings.
It is the first official papal visit to France in 18 years.
Pope Leo asked those in the crowd not to keep their faith to themselves. “Let it overflow, so that those you meet may be refreshed and their thirst satisfied,” he said. “From this beautiful city of Paris, I pray fervently that the living water of the Holy Spirit may flow throughout France.”
He told Catholics that only their faith, and not material things, can provide true happiness.
“Only God can fill the emptiness within us,” he said.
The security zone for the event – the biggest of the papal tour – stretched about 1.4 miles (2.2km), shutting down road traffic in central Paris from the Place de la Concorde to the Arc de Triomphe and beyond.
Chanting “Leo, Leo” and “Long live the pope”, crowds of people waved French and Vatican flags as the pontiff rode slowly down the grand boulevard of the Champs-Élysées aboard a popemobile – a specially designed, partly open vehicle used during public appearances.
He stopped frequently along the way as babies were lifted out of the crowd and brought to him to receive a papal caress on their heads. The city centre was sealed off for the service, with helicopters circling overhead and snipers positioned on rooftops.
About 14,500 police officers, gendarmes, military personnel and firefighters were deployed to the event, which was attended by 2,400 priests and deacons, and about 100 bishops.
Marie-Élisabeth, a 44-year-old nun from Burgundy, told a reporter for France 24: “This event is a way for us to say loud and proud that Christians are here.”
Speaking to reporters from Agence France-Presse, Sylvie Leclerc, a 51-year-old teacher, also said she and her fellow Christians want to share their fervour for their faith. “You don’t hear much from us Catholics, but now we’re going to make some noise!” she said. “But to proclaim love, peace, joy.”

Uzbekistan held on to its sole lead with 18 points, while India continued to pursue closely behind on 17 points after the 10th and penultimate round of the 46th Chess Olympiad 2026 . Uzbekistan and India scored dominating 3.5-0.5 victories over Armenia and Uzbekistan 2, respectively. Germany, Ukraine, and Hungary all follow the leaders with 16 points, after defeating France, China, and Spain, respectively.
In the 2026 FIDE Women's Chess Olympiad , China and India had a thrilling draw with scores tied at 2-2 at the end of a match of fluctuating fortunes. Kazakhstan jumped to second place with 17 points after an unexpected 2.5-1.5 win over France. China with 18 points and Kazakhstan with 17 points are in the top two places in the points table. They are followed by India, Poland, and Vietnam with 16 points apiece.
Thus, both sections promise last-round action, which will settle the quest for medals.
The 11th and final round will be on Sunday, September 27, starting at 2:15 a.m. ET / 8:15 CEST / 11:45 a.m. IST.

Just as the event enters its most crucial phase, there is no question that the team captains are at their most pressed selves, and they have their own ways of coping with the tension.
📖♟ Which book would you choose to read during the round? Being a captain at the FIDE Chess Olympiad can be stressful. #ChessOlympiad pic.twitter.com/Lo16YNRD5l
But it was a different story for spectators, as the final rounds bring the best of the excitement of watching tense games.
Uzbekistan and India scored smooth victories to still keep alive the fight for medals till the last round. For the former, GMs Nodirbek Abdusattorov , Javokhir Sindarov , and Mukhiddin Madaminov scored victories.
In any team tournament, common advice to players would be not to play in a way that worries the other members of the unit. But soon after the round started, the top three players of the Uzbekistan team looked determined to ignore the diktat. Abdusattorov adopted the unorthodox Scandinavian Defense with Black, Sindarov uncorked the sacrifice of an exchange, and GM Nodirbek Yakubboev had given up the center to his opponent.
Abdusattorov defended patiently in the middlegame and the early endgame and exploited his chances in a subtle endgame involving rooks and bishops of opposite color.
The most exciting game of the match was between Sindarov and GM Robert Hovhannisyan , where the world championship challenger sacrificed an exchange early in the game to set up an exciting middlegame, where he had a knight and two pawns for his opponent's rook. This is our Game of the Day, analyzed by GM Rafael Leitao below.
In the other two games of the match, Yakubboev drew with GM Shant Sargsyan , while Madaminov defeated GM Gabriel Sargissian .
It was GM Nihal Sarin who provided the first break for India, winning a game where he held the advantage from the get-go.
🔥 BREAKING: 🇮🇳 GM Nihal Sarin scored a crucial win against 🇺🇿 GM Suyarov! 📸 @FIDE_chess / Michal Walusza #ChessOlympiad pic.twitter.com/vCc0rZj3TB
World champion GM Gukesh Dommaraju seemed to be playing somewhat uncharacteristically, opting for the quiet London System for this crucial game. He continued playing in the same way, playing a measured game where he increased his advantage systematically to win deservingly after 47 moves.
On the top board too, GM Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa outwitted GM Jakhongir Vakhidov in a major-pieces endgame, while GM Arjun Erigaisi vs. GM Abdimalik Abdisalimov ended in a draw.
Against China, the crucial win for Ukraine came on the top board when GM Igor Kovalenko defeated former world champion GM Ding Liren , while 18-year-old IM Roman Dehtiarov defeated 17-year-old GM Xiangrui Kong .
Germany's win over France was achieved thanks to brothers and GMs Frederik Svane and Rasmus Svane triumphing over GMs Maxime Lagarde and Marc'Andria Maurizzi , respectively.
All the encounters of the Hungary-Spain match ended decisively, with the crucial win for the former coming through a long-drawn endgame by GM Richard Rapport.
An important matchup of the day was between two of the most exciting contemporary prodigies of the game—the 15-year-old GM Yagiz Erdogmus of Turkiye, the youngest ever to reach Elo 2700, and 12-year-old GM Faustino Oro of Argentina, the youngest grandmaster in the world currently .
Talking to Chess.com's FM Mike Klein after his win, Erdogmus displayed his maturity and ambitiousness with measured words.
On breaking the record for youngest 2700: "I'm giving a lot of time to chess, I mean I think I deserve these records. I'm giving my best all the time." On the game vs. Faustino Oro: "I was focusing on the game, not the opponent." -Yagiz Erdogmus #ChessOlympiad pic.twitter.com/sCr5OUFJ1a
Final Round Pairings: Top 10 Open
Round 10 Results | Women's Top 10
Women's Standings After Round 10: Top 20
The top encounter between China and India was the highlight of the round, as the latter looked to level the difference in scores by winning the match. The Indians definitely had hopes on the lower boards, as both IMs Vantika Agrawal and Savitha Shri were undefeated till this point, with individual scores of 5.5/6 and 7.5/8 points, respectively, in the tournament. Of course, Vantika faced IM Lu Miaoyi who had scored 7.5/9 and Savitha faced WGM Zhai Mo who had scored 4.5/6 till this point of the tournament. But a curious and important factor of these two encounters was that all four players had stayed undefeated till this time.
The tense China-India matchup seemed to have its first casualty when the best player for her country so far in the tournament blundered a pawn in an equal position.
"This happened, unfortunately, in the biggest match of all!" says David Howell as Savitha Shri blunders a pawn in the match of India vs. China! https://t.co/khMEvfSfsi #ChessOlympiad pic.twitter.com/D4y9taykRp
But subsequently, the game went through so many twists and turns, resulting in commentator GM Robert Hess exclaiming, "This game is giving everybody heart palpitations!"
This game is giving everybody heart palpitations!
At this point, the top two encounters of the match were proceeding peacefully, while Lu-Vantika was an almost level game where the latter was defending a slightly inconvenient position.
But as time went on, Vantika got into trouble in an endgame and went on to lose.
But Savitha fought back into the game, and it ended in her favor after many twists and turns.
Thanks to this dramatic encounter, India managed to level the scores with a 2-2 result.
France seemed to be winning this encounter comfortably, as IMs Sophie Millet and Pauline Guichard were seemingly enjoying a huge advantage in their respective games. This was after the top board encounter between Kazakh GM Bibisara Assaubayeva 's game had ended in her favor against IM Deimante Daulyte-Cornette .
However, after Millet did win her game, the other game produced a huge blind spot for Guichard who blundered and lost to 16-year-old IM Elnaz Kaliakhmet .
Kazakhstan wins the match after Pauline Guichard, up a piece, blunders her rook! https://t.co/4JXuUTiAwE #ChessOlympiad pic.twitter.com/8hf1N0ZYTY
Thus, Kazakhstan defeated France to climb up the standings and landed in second place behind leader China, with a total of 17 points. They are followed by India, Poland, and Vietnam, all with 16 points in the final standings.

articles.title_zh: White House Blocks CNN From Air Force One, Networks Suspend Pool Coverage Again
articles.content_orig:
CNN had been scheduled to fly with Trump on Air Force One
Broadcaster CNN has been barred from travelling with US President Donald Trump on Air Force One for a trip to Tennessee on Saturday.
The move is the latest in a battle between the White House and the media after it was forced to lift its ban on some news outlets.
CNN was scheduled to fly with Trump for his trip to Tennessee for a college American football game until a note released on Friday night by the White House did not list the broadcaster on the media schedule.
The BBC has requested comment from the White House.
CNN has reported that no other outlet was listed as replacing them in the president's tentative schedule.
Last week, Trump banned CNN, Politico and MS NOW journalists from the White House after accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration.
All three media outlets said they were pursuing legal action and accused Trump of violating their constitutional rights to free speech and freedom of the press.
Four television networks that have a daily rotation of White House coverage alongside CNN - ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC - had paused their broadcasts of the president in solidarity with the banned outlets.
The White House then launched its own streaming channel, Trump TV, ahead of the UN General Assembly in New York.
A federal judge has since ruled that Trump barring news outlets from the White House was likely unconstitutional and that the administration had to let them back in, at least for now.
However, the White House still denied entry to some CNN and MS NOW reporters assigned to cover arrivals at a state dinner for Chinese leader Xi Jinping on Thursday.
In a series of online posts on Saturday, Trump criticised the CNN and other media outlets dubbing them "fake news".
"FAKE NEWS SHOULD NOT BE ALLOWED IN THE WHITE HOUSE," he said.
A White House communications account earlier posted on X that "contrary to what the Fake News wants you to believe, they don't just get to have free rein into every part of the White House, every event and every press call".
Regular US television coverage resumed on Friday after White House officials allowed reporters entry.
The president is set to attend a football game between University of Tennessee vs University of Texas College at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville from midday local time on Saturday.

articles.title_orig: Trump says he has rejected Iranian proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
articles.title_zh: Trump says he has rejected Iranian proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
articles.content_orig:
President Donald Trump said Saturday that he has rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, after Iranian officials indicated that shipping through the critical waterway could resume within days if a deal was sealed.
“I rejected their deal. They want to make a deal where they open the strait immediately because they’re losing so badly,” Trump told reporters as he boarded Marine One on the White House lawn, after indirect talks between the two countries were held on the sidelines of this week’s United Nations General Assembly in New York.
“What they wanted is to immediately open the Hormuz Strait. You know why? Because they’re dying. You know why they’re dying? Because they have no money coming in because they get their money from the Hormuz Strait,” he continued. “They outsmarted themselves. They said, ‘Let’s close it and cause a problem for the world.’ And I came along, and we put up the greatest blockade ever in military history.”
The Wall Street Journal first reported that Trump had rejected Iran’s offer to revive a ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz .
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had said Friday that the choice “rests with the United States.”
“If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened and normal maritime passage restored within seven days,” Araghchi told reporters.
He said a “concrete seven-day plan” that includes reopening the strait had been conveyed to the U.S. through mediator Qatar and was ready to start “as soon as the United States accepts this plan.”
Iran offers new proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
Araghchi said the actions required of the U.S. in Iran’s proposal were commitments already agreed to in the June memorandum of understanding between the two countries that laid out plans for a temporary ceasefire. That agreement, signed in June, collapsed within days after fresh strikes were exchanged.
One of the conditions of the plan is for the U.S. to accept a maritime transit route through the Strait of Hormuz that has been agreed upon by Iran and Oman , Araghchi had said Thursday.
A U.S. official said on Friday that the Trump administration was having positive and constructive discussions through the mediators but that it was not in any hurry to reach an agreement.
“The United States is in a very strong position with control of the Strait of Hormuz, so we are not in a rush,” the U.S. official said. “Over the last 48 hours, nearly 40 million barrels of oil have transited the strait.”
Earlier this week, Trump said he was still considering whether to “annihilate” Iran or make a deal. Early Saturday, he posted an image to Truth Social of the Strait of Hormuz labeled the “Trump Strait.”
In an interview with Al Jazeera on Saturday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said that resolving the Hormuz issue “is possible through negotiations, not the use of force,” but warned that his country does not “trust” talks with Washington.
Trump has repeatedly said that the goal of attacking Iran was to prevent the development of a nuclear weapon. Soon after the war started, Iran blocked the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway through which some 20% of the world’s oil flowed before the conflict, sending shock waves through the world economy.
Pezeshkian on Thursday suggested his government was willing to make a deal with the U.S. to end the war before Americans head to the polls this November.
“We don’t want it to get to the midterm elections,” Pezeshkian said in a brief meeting with NBC News and other news organizations, two days after Trump said he believed the Iranian regime would not make a deal to settle the conflict until after the elections .
“I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to,” Trump said. “They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election.”
Polls show Democrats with an advantage heading into the November midterms. The latest NBC News Decision Desk Poll found 31% of respondents approved of Trump’s handling of the Iran war, while 69% disapproved.
The U.S. this week announced it would impose sanctions on any global companies doing business ​with Iranian airlines, with the aim of grounding Iran’s entire civil fleet worldwide.
Iraq said Saturday that it was engaging with the U.S. in an effort to restore humanitarian flights to and from Iran, after Iranian airlines were barred from neighboring countries in response to the sanctions.
Efforts were ongoing to “secure exemptions for certain Iraqi airports from these measures” in order to enable “the resumption of flights for humanitarian reasons, such as medical treatment, education, religious pilgrimages, and the interests of civilians,” the Iraqi prime minister’s office said.
Iran’s Tasnim news agency reported that flights had also been shut down to Oman, Georgia and Azerbaijan.

By CHRIS MELORE, US DEPUTY SCIENCE EDITOR
Published: 10:00 EDT, 26 September 2026 | Updated: 11:00 EDT, 26 September 2026
Hurricane Nolo is expected to cause 'catastrophic flooding' as the life-threatening storm nears the Hawaiian islands and over one million Americans this weekend.
A state of emergency has already been issued in Hawaii and forecasters now believe the strengthening hurricane could bring historic levels of rainfall, particularly across the Big Island (also known as Hawaii Island).
AccuWeather forecasters warned that the week-long deluge could dump as much as 55 inches of rain on the Big Island - just under five feet of precipitation.
If that prediction is correct, Nolo would be the second wettest hurricane in Hawaii's history, falling just behind Hurricane Lane's 58 inches in 2018.
The National Hurricane Center (NHC) said in a statement: 'Life-threatening, catastrophic flooding and mudslides are possible, especially in areas of steep terrain across the eastern and southern portions of the Big Island and Maui.'
Local officials on the islands have also urged residents and tourists to be prepared to evacuate flood-prone areas as the hurricane makes its closest approach.
Although Nolo is not projected to make landfall, AccuWeather has projected that at least two to four inches of rain will fall across the entire island chain. The hurricane is currently about 140 miles from Hawaii.
Both Maui and the Big Island are also expected to be struck by dangerous and sustained wind gusts reaching between 60 and 80 mph through Monday.
Hurricane Nolo is expected to become a Category 4 hurricane this weekend with winds over 130 mph
Residents in Hawaii began preparing for potentially catastrophic flooding this week
Nolo erupted into a tropical storm on Wednesday less than 400 miles south of the Hawaiian islands and has been slowly gaining strength throughout the week.
AccuWeather and NHC have both warned that Nolo will likely reach major hurricane status by Saturday afternoon, growing into a Category 3 storm with sustained winds exceeding 111 mph.
Saturday is expected to be the peak of the threat for Hawaii, as the hurricane makes its closest approach to land.
The worst of the rain and possible hurricane-force winds are expected to hit the exposed slopes of the Big Island's eastern side. Forecasts have predicted that this side of the island will see at least two feet of rain.
Maui, a major tourist destination just 30 miles to the west of the Big Island, will also see increasing rain and possible tropical storm conditions on Saturday, as winds range between 40 and 60 mph.
Mayor Richard Bissen of Maui County said in a statement : 'During this above-normal hurricane season, recent storms remind us that we cannot afford to be complacent.'
'Our top priority is the safety of our community. Now is the time for all of us to review household emergency plans, check supplies and make sure you can receive important alerts and information.'
National Weather Service officials in Honolulu warned: 'Leave immediately if evacuation orders are given for your area.'
Hurricane Lala caused at least two deaths and billions of dollars in damage from flooding and mudslides in August
Forecasters have warned that more than three feet of rain could fall on Hawaii's Big Island
A prediction of 55 inches of rain by AccuWeather would make Hurricane Nolo the second wettest hurricane in Hawaii's history
Hawaii's Big Island is home to more than 200,000 people, and the island is still recovering from the devastating effects of Hurricanes Lala and Lowell this summer.
The storm destroyed over 100 homes, damaged hundreds more and killed at least five people across the state, with the heaviest damage occurring on the Big Island during Lala's approach on August 15.
Downpours, flooding and mudslides, similar to what is expected during Nolo, led to more than 100 homes on the Big Island being washed away during the August hurricane.
Hurricane Lowell struck the opposite end of the island chain in September, causing widespread power outages and property damage on the islands of Kauaʻi and Niʻihau.
Emergency shelters have been opened on the Big Island ahead of the hurricane's arrival.
Hawaii County Mayor Kimo Alameda said in a statement: 'If your home flooded before, or is at risk, consider moving to safer shelter before the full force of the storm hits. Because the ground remains saturated, flooding may happen rapidly.'
By Sunday, Nolo is expected to start moving away from Hawaii, although the hurricane will likely continue strengthening, growing into a Category 4 storm with winds surpassing 130 mph.
Rain and flooding will likely continue before gradually easing heading into the new week.

articles.title_zh: German town bans 'stumbling stone' memorials to Nazi victims
articles.content_orig:
"Stumbling stone" memorials - like the one pictured in the Netherlands - are often placed in memory of Jews and other victims of the Holocaust
There has been a wave of criticism in Germany after the town of Heidenau, near Dresden in Saxony, decided to ban "stumbling stone" memorials to victims of the Nazis.
Germany's Education Minister Karin Prien told newspaper Bild that the ban was a "scandal".
Since the 1990s, many towns in countries across Europe, including in Germany and Austria, have embedded small brass plaques in the streets in memory of Jews and other victims of Nazi atrocities.
The plaques, called Stolpersteine in German, are often placed outside the houses where the victims used to live or work. They are frequently funded by donations.
But now councillors from the Alternative fÃ¼r Deutschland (AfD) party and the conservative CDU in Heidenau have voted to ban stumbling stones in their town.
The AfD in Saxony has been classified as extreme-right by German intelligence, a designation the party rejects.
The motion in the town council said that many citizens felt that this form of commemoration of Nazi victims was inappropriate.
Memorials should in future be placed at the city's Nordfriedhof cemetery to make it "impossible to step directly onto the memorial elements", the motion stated.
Stumbling stones placed near the Reichstag in Berlin
However, Karin Prien, a member of the CDU, criticised the decision.
"Anyone who banishes Stolpersteine and memorial sites commemorating Jewish life from public spaces to the cemetery is prioritising death over life and rendering Jewish people invisible once again," she told Bild.
She said her own CDU party in Saxony also bore responsibility for the decision.
Charlotte Knobloch, a Holocaust survivor and president of the Jewish Community in Munich, said that removing memorials from the cityscape was "completely the wrong approach".
She told the Funke Media Group that she was "appalled that a democratic party would stoop to supporting such a transparent manoeuvre by the extremists of the AfD".
Knobloch said that she was not a supporter of the stumbling stones, but added that "decentralised remembrance â which is not banished from public space but, on the contrary, permeates and shapes it" was crucial to a genuine culture of remembrance.
In her own city of Munich, there are no Stolpersteine on municipal land. Instead, the city allows memorial plaques on public buildings.
As the name suggests, Stolpersteine are intended as memorials people stumble upon, making them reflect on the history of their location.
Gunter Demnig, the artist who initiated the Stolperstein project, said that given the recent electoral successes of the AfD "it was certainly to be expected that something like this would happen".
The AfD recently secured major victories in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.
Some branches of the populist AfD are classed as right-wing extremist by domestic intelligence, a designation the party strongly rejects.
Its anti-immigration, "Germany first" and Russian-friendly agenda has found fertile ground in the country's former communist east.

Investors looking to boost their exposure to artificial intelligence should target China, according to Matthews Asia portfolio manager Andrew Mattock.
He said investors will need a more deliberate approach because broad emerging market strategies won't be that effective.
"Investors need to be aware when they buy an emerging market fund or when they buy a plain vanilla MSCI product… they're not getting a lot of it," Mattock told CNBC's "ETF Edge" this week. "The big piece that you are missing… is the Chinese piece."
He noted that companies from South Korea and Taiwan comprise almost half of the iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF (EEM) while the iShares MSCI China ETF (MCHI) lacks a focus on AI stocks.
Mattock is behind the Matthews China Fund (MCHFX) . The fund invests at least 80% of its net assets in  the common and preferred stocks of companies located in China, according to the firm's website.
The fund is off 4% so far this year, as of Friday's close. Its largest holdings include Tencent and Alibaba .
It appears investing in China is seeing a meaningful shift.
Billionaire hedge fund manager David Tepper, founder of Appaloosa Management, found the world's second economy attractive again – telling CNBC in September 2024 that he bought more of "everything" related to China.
However, KraneShares' Brendan Ahern recommended that investors consider strategies that could protect them from wild market swings in China.
"I like the idea of utilizing options around some of those ETFs…  like with KWEB [KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF]," the firm's chief investment officer said in the same interview.
"Why do some of these hedge funds gravitate to these ETFs? Because they're able to write a call and principally protect themselves," he added. "Give themselves some downside."
According to FactSet, the KraneShares CSI China Internet ETF has the same top two holdings as the Matthews China Fund: Tencent and Alibaba. But as of Friday's close, the fund is down more than 27% so far this year.

articles.title_orig: Body of 10th woman found in South Africa as killings investigation continues
articles.title_zh: Body of 10th woman found in South Africa as killings investigation continues
articles.content_orig:
South African police said Saturday that another woman's body had been found near Johannesburg, bringing the number of victims to 10 in a series of killings under investigation.
Police began investigating after the bodies of three women were found in July and August within about 4.3 miles of one another in the Ekurhuleni municipality, east of Johannesburg.
The discovery of six bodies in Ekurhuleni over 10 days earlier this month raised fears that a serial killer or killers were responsible.
Two women were arrested and charged last week with murder in relation to the ninth body , discovered on Sept. 17. The victim had been stabbed and had her throat cut, police said. Police did not link the two women charged to any of the other killings.
Provincial police commissioner Lt. Gen. Tommy Mthombeni told state broadcaster SABC on Saturday that investigators believed the ninth killing was an isolated case but could not rule out the possibility that some of the other cases were linked.
Police had issued a warning for women to use caution while in the area.
Police have identified similarities in some of the killings but said they had not found conclusive evidence that the same person or people were responsible.
All nine of the bodies discovered before Saturday were those of women in their 20s or 30s, according to police. Several were naked or partially clothed and left in open areas near main roads. Officers from the Investigative Psychology Unit, which specializes in complex or serial violent crimes, are part of the investigation.
Police released limited details about the 10th body, which was found early Saturday, and did not immediately identify the victim.
"We can only confirm the discovery of the body," the South African Police Service said in a statement. "Crime scene management and all the necessary role players are currently on the scene."
South Africa has high rates of violent crime and violence against women. Three women were killed every day by an intimate partner from 2020-2021, a recent study found.
The country has one of the highest global murder rates , with more than 60 a day on average.
The killings in Ekurhuleni have sparked a national outcry over women's safety.

articles.title_orig: White House blocks CNN from traveling with Trump on Air Force One
articles.title_zh: White House blocks CNN from traveling with Trump on Air Force One
articles.content_orig:
The White House is barring CNN from flying on Air Force One on Saturday as part of the news outlet’s duties covering the president on behalf of major television networks.
CNN had been scheduled to fly aboard the president’s plane on his trip to Tennessee for a college football game as part of the White House TV press pool — a small, rotating group of journalists that cover the president in areas where space is limited and share the information they gather with other TV networks.
The move — announced Friday night in a White House note that lays out the president’s schedule — represents the Trump administration’s latest salvo against CNN and the broader White House press corps. No outlet was listed as replacing CNN, meaning there will be no television pool coverage of his trip.
Last week, President Donald Trump announced he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. The move also prevented CNN from flying on Air Force One and fulfilling its scheduled pool duties when Trump traveled to the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
A judge later blocked the administration from enforcing the White House ban on the three outlets and ordered it to restore the credentials of the affected reporters. The status of the White House pool, though, was murkier.
With CNN banned, the other TV outlets — Fox, NBC, ABC and CBS — refused to perform their duties until regular access was restored. But regular coverage resumed on Friday, with CNN serving as part of the pool as Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping visited the National Archives.
It was unclear how the White House’s move might affect CNN, MS NOW and Politico’s litigation. The outside lawyer representing CNN had previously told anchor Jake Tapper he believed the restoration of the outlets’ access included the White House pool. MS NOW and Politico are a part of separate pool rotations from the five major TV networks.
A judge has given the news organizations until Monday to file a request for a preliminary injunction — which would put Trump’s promised ban on hold for a longer period of time.
A CNN spokesperson declined to comment. CNN has reached out to the White House for comment.
In two posts on Truth Social Saturday morning, Trump said CNN and MS NOW should not be allowed in the White House, calling the organizations “perpetrators of FAKE NEWS.”
Later that morning, as he took questions from reporters while departing for Knoxville, an MS NOW reporter asked Trump if he only wants outlets that support him to be part of the White House press pool, to which Trump responded, “I want real news, not fake news.”
“I love an open, free press. What I don’t like is the fake press,” Trump said as he singled out MS NOW and CNN. “What we don’t want is — we don’t want fake news.”
The Washington Post was first to report the White House’s decision.
The TV pool is the primary way that people around the world watch Trump’s speeches and appearances because it supplies video feeds and information to other news organizations.
“That’s the system that allows the networks to share video of the president with the whole country. If they aren’t there, the pool can’t function,” the current president of the White House Correspondents’ Association, Jacqui Heinrich, said on “Fox News Sunday.”
“And America cannot have state TV,” her guest Weijia Jiang of CBS, who was Heinrich’s predecessor as WHCA president, said.
“That’s what makes America America,” she said. “That’s why we need independent coverage, and that’s why this press pool system has been set up for so long and why it works – because you need independent actors to be able to be the observers.”
Along with the TV pool, there are also print, radio and still photography pools. This system exists partly because presidents travel and speak in places where the wider press corps cannot be present.
The Trump White House also produces its own content, including live streams of events.
But, as Jiang put it, “if the government is only showing you what it wants, then you have to question, what are we missing? And that’s what the pool, that’s what these outlets bring to the table.”
This story has been updated with additional details.

The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Saturday (September 26, 2026) announced a slew of measures addressing concerns over the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls across the country, including stopping physical hearings for unmapped voters or those with logical discrepancies in their enumeration forms.
It said that the declaration accompanying Form 6 (used for fresh voter registration) is mandatory only during the current SIR process. This in effect means that new voters who seek inclusion in electoral rolls after the ongoing SIR need not submit any such declaration.
The commission also said that any person whose name has got left out during SIR or thereafter, and any person including young/ first-time voters, may apply to the electoral registration officer (ERO) concerned, for inclusion of their names in the electoral rolls.  A special drive will immediately be launched for their enrolment, it said in a press note.
The SIR process has already been completed in 20 States and Union Territories.
The fresh initiatives of the poll body came after a meeting of the full bench of the commission on Saturday afternoon (September 26, 2026) and days after reports emerged of a rift within the Election Commissioners over these and other issues in the SIR process as well as the internal working of the ECI.
The press note confirmed that the two Commissioners had written to the Cabinet Secretary but said it was not related to any policy matter of the commission or IT division but related to working of an officer on deputation to the ECI. “The work re-distribution orders issued by the concerned officer were not actually implemented after the orders of the two Commissioners,” it clarified.
The commission’s press note was pertinently accompanied by a photograph of all the three Election Commissioners and mentioned that it “has the approval of the full commission”.
As far as physical hearings were concerned, the statement said: “In case of any person to whom notice has been issued during the ongoing SIR, for being unmapped and for logical discrepancies, BLOs (booth-level officers) will visit the homes of such persons for collection of documents and thereafter upload them on the ECINet, for decision by the ERO.”
“Such persons need not be called for hearing to ERO/AERO office. Only in exceptional circumstances, as decided by the ERO, the hearing will be held preferably online. Any adult member of the family can be authorised by the elector to attend the hearing on their behalf, if required. Facilities for the online hearing are to be strengthened.”
As regards new voter registration, the EC maintained that the declaration form attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Supreme Court, but for non-SIR period, the forms appFmahalicable as per rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used for new voter inclusion.

The other issue that had attracted the ire of the two Election Commissioners was the supposed centralisation of management of voter rolls through the ECINet portal, with field officers unable to access it in many cases.
The statement said that “A Committee headed by Sr. Deputy Election Commissioner (DEC) and including an independent expert from IIT/IIIT will review the ECINET to double-check that it complies with the provisions of the Acts and Rules and submit report to the Commission”. It added that henceforth, all the new initiatives about IT modules and portals will be discussed in the Committee of Officers (COO) before approval by the commission.
“Field officers have role-based access to the ECINET system as per their statutory powers. In case, any further flexibility is required by the field officers, that will be made operational,” it added.
The commission also extended the period for filing claims and objections for Delhi till October 30 and for Maharashtra till October 12.
Many other administrative measures were also announced. These include circulation of an advanced agenda and issuance of minutes for all of Commission’s meetings, completion of annual performance appraisal reports of all the officers within the stipulated time frame, approval of the commission for foreign trips of officers and compliance with all directions issued by the Commissioners to the officers of the Commission.
The Opposition, which has been seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, remained unimpressed with the statement. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said: “The CEC thinks he can hide behind protocol. He stands exposed and is now petrified as an entire country seeks to hold him accountable.”
“The ongoing SIR which has turned to be method of massive disenfranchisement of several crores of India must be suspended immediately without delay. In the meantime, nothing short of the CEC’s resignation or prosecution will suffice”.

articles.title_orig: White House Removes CNN From Planned Weekend Trip
articles.title_zh: White House Removes CNN From Planned Weekend Trip
articles.content_orig:
The White House on Friday night removed CNN from joining President Donald Trump on his trip to Tennessee on Saturday, where it was supposed to cover the president on behalf of major TV networks.
According to media guidance sent out by the White House on Friday night, CNN was removed from the list of outlets designated for pool coverage of Trump’s trip, in which he is set to attend a college football game in Knoxville.
The pool is a rotating group of networks that share duties of filming the president both in Washington and on official trips. Other member networks — Fox News, ABC News, CBS News and NBC News — briefly boycotted participating in the pool this week after Trump banned CNN from serving as a member.
CNN on Friday reported that it had been scheduled to fly with Trump on Air Force One on Saturday as part of its pool duties covering the president’s trip to the game between the University of Texas and the University of Tennessee. However in the president’s schedule released Friday night, CNN was not listed as a member of the pool and no other network was listed as replacing it.
The move is the latest development in the White House’s attempt to restrict access by CNN and other outlets to cover the White House. The president last week had banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico from accessing the White House before a judge temporarily blocked that move Thursday and ordered the administration to restore their reporters’ credentials for 14 days.
But while the order restored the outlets’ access to the White House, it didn’t explicitly require the administration to restore CNN’s participation in the television pool.
The White House did not immediately return a request for comment.

articles.title_orig: At Summit, Xi Sought to Tilt Trump’s Stance on America’s Place in Asia
articles.title_zh: At Summit, Xi Sought to Tilt Trump’s Stance on America’s Place in Asia
articles.content_orig:
Donald Trump's dinner with China's leader, Xi Jinping, on Thursday was a glitzy gathering of the biggest names in tech.
AMD CEO Lisa Su said during a fireside chat at the New York Stock Exchange that she will be attending Thursday's White House event, joining executives expected to include Nvidia's Jensen Huang, OpenAI's Sam Altman, Alphabet's Sundar Pichai, Tesla's Elon Musk, and Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.
Dario Amodei, the Anthropic CEO who also led the call for more cautious AI development, was notably absent from the dinner.
Plenty is riding on the talks. Washington and Beijing are negotiating amid a trade truce, with tariffs, critical minerals, and semiconductors among the issues at stake. The US has also proposed a channel for the two countries to notify each other about significant AI safety incidents, which remains under discussion.
"I think technology is one of those areas where we rely on the global ecosystem to come together," Su told Fox Business's Liz Claman in a fireside chat on Wednesday, adding she was "honored" to join the White House dinner.
"So, yes, I think we're anxiously looking at what will come out of it," Su said. "And the truth is, we want to ensure that there's good stability across the global ecosystem as it relates to technology."
In clockwise order, Trump's table consisted of himself, first lady Melania Trump, Musk, Su and her spouse, Daniel Lin, Jensen Huang and his spouse, Lori Huang, former Apple CEO Tim Cook , China's first lady Peng Liyuan, and China's leader Xi Jinping.
Vice President JD Vance and Usha Vance were seen seated at a different table to the right.
The two tech CEOs have both recently weighed in on AI safety issues, as the topic is expected to be discussed with China's leader.
Altman has backed setting shared safety standards, including rules for when companies should slow or stop developing more powerful models, while Zuckerberg has said that AI labs have strong incentives to make their models safe and can decide for themselves when to slow down.
Huang, dressed in more traditional business attire, was seated at the main table alongside Trump and Xi.
Nvidia has felt the tech rivalry between the US and China acutely over the past few years. After Washington imposed new export restrictions on Nvidia's H20 chips in April 2025, the company said it missed out on $2.5 billion in shipments that quarter and took a $4.5 billion charge tied to unsold inventory and purchase commitments.
As recently as August, Nvidia was still assuming no China data center chip revenue in its forecast.
Musk and Brockman, the spouse of OpenAI cofounder and president Greg Brockman, are both heavyweight Trump donors.
Musk, in particular, holds major business interests in China due to Tesla's Gigafactory in Shanghai , which produces about half of the automaker's deliveries.
The world's richest man said earlier this month, during a podcast appearance, that the US and China should agree to peer review or test AI models from the leading firms in each other's countries.
Musk's SpaceX is also arguably the single most important company to the US space race against China, providing the bulk of American orbital launches and maintaining the world's largest satellite constellation.
The Google CEO was seen having an animated conversation with Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
Google, one of the leading AI labs in the US, is investing heavily in AI capacity, with a total capex forecast of $195 billion to $205 billion this year. That's higher than most of the rest of Big Tech, except for Amazon , which estimates $220 billion in total capex in 2026.
Amazon doesn't operate its marketplace in China, which has its own, far more domestically successful e-commerce platforms.
But the country has become a major supply and export hub for Amazon, to the point that the company built a global warehousing and distribution network this year in three major Chinese shipping ports to funnel goods to the US.
Bezos and Sánchez were just two representatives of America's corporate elite invited to Thursday's dinner — lead executives for BlackRock, JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs, LVMH, and Lockheed Martin were also among those present.

President Donald Trump lashed out over his press coverage again Saturday morning after a federal judge ordered him to immediately lift a White House ban on CNN, Politico and MS NOW.
In two early morning Truth Social posts, Trump questioned why journalists should have access to the “very sacred” White House. The posts came shortly after his administration barred CNN from Air Force One Saturday and replaced the outlet with LindellTV for his trip to Knoxville, Tennessee, to attend a college football game.
“Why should perpetrators of FAKE NEWS, like CNN and MSDNC, be allowed access to a very sacred place, the White House?” Trump demanded. “Despite my big Election Win, almost 100% of ‘TRUMP’ coverage is negative, and has been for years!”
Less than two hours later, Trump escalated his criticism.
“FAKE NEWS SHOULD NOT BE ALLOWED IN THE WHITE HOUSE!!! IT HAS GONE ON FAR TOO LONG, AT A TREMENDOUS COST TO OUR COUNTRY,” he wrote.
The latest clash with the media began September 18, when Trump abruptly announced that CNN, MS NOW and Politico would be barred from the White House . According to reports, the ban came hours after his aide Natalie Harp showed him videos of unflattering news coverage.
“Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they’re covering the President of the United States, the Trump Administration, or the United States of America,” he wrote on Truth Social. “Other Fake News Media Outlets to follow.”
By the following morning, CNN, MS NOW and Politico all said that their journalists had been stopped from accessing the White House grounds, with some reporters saying that they were asked to hand over their badges.
On September 21, the outlets filed a lawsuit against Trump and several of his top aides, arguing that the ban violates the Fifth Amendment’s Due Process Clause, as well as the First Amendment, and calls for the press passes to be restored.
“This ban could not be a more direct assault on the First Amendment nor a more blatant violation of our most fundamental constitutional principles,” the lawsuit states.
The Justice Department has argued that Trump has the authority to ban the outlets on “ national security ” grounds, claiming that “access to the White House is a privilege—not a right.”
On September 24, U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly ordered the Trump administration to temporarily reinstate the outlets’ press badges. By that afternoon, reporters regained access to the White House .
Yet, on September 25, the White House announced that CNN will not be allowed on Air Force One when Trump flies to Knoxville, Tennessee, on Saturday for a college football game, the network reported .
CNN is part of a rotating press pool that covers White House events for major TV networks.
Instead, the White House listed LindellTV, a conservative online video platform founded by Trump ally Mike Lindell , on the Air Force One Saturday schedule. Real America’s Voice was also listed.
“I love an open free press,” Trump told reporters Saturday morning before departing from the White House on Marine One.
“What I don’t like is fake news, and they’re fake news 100 percent,” he said, referring to the three outlets he banned. “In two years I doubt they did one good story.”
Trump has long had an extremely combative relationship with the press , accusing reporters of unfair and biased coverage, lobbing personal insults against them and insinuating that those he opposes should be punished.
The president previously curtailed The Associated Press from accessing certain presidential spaces in 2025 after the outlet continued using the “Gulf of Mexico” despite Trump rebranding it as the “Gulf of America.” In 2018, Trump also revoked CNN reporter Jim Acosta’s press pass following a contentious news conference.

articles.title_orig: Is Ethiopia on the verge of another civil war as fighting erupts in Tigray?
articles.title_zh: Is Ethiopia on the verge of another civil war as fighting erupts in Tigray?
articles.content_orig:
Intensified fighting between Ethiopia’s federal army and forces from the northern region of Tigray has raised fears that the peace agreement that ended a devastating two-year war in 2022 could collapse.
The escalation came days after seven armed groups from across Ethiopia formed a new alliance which seeks to remove Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government, with each side of the conflict blaming the other for instigating the latest flare-up in violence.
The immediate fear for many in the country is a return to the war they have spent nearly four years trying to recover from. Here is what we know.
The Tigray People’s Liberation Front, or TPLF, began as an armed movement against Ethiopia’s military government in the 1970s. It later became the dominant force in the coalition that governed Ethiopia for nearly three decades.
That influence was contentious in a country with many ethnic groups, where Tigrayans account for only about 6 percent of Ethiopia’s population. When Abiy became prime minister in 2018, he created the Prosperity Party to replace the governing coalition, sharply reducing the TPLF’s influence at the centre of government.
Relations between Abiy’s government and the TPLF deteriorated until war broke out in November 2020. Federal troops, Eritrean forces and some fighters from the neighbouring Amhara region fought against Tigrayan forces. The conflict killed hundreds of thousands of people, displaced millions and left Tigray largely cut off from the outside world.
A peace agreement signed in Pretoria, South Africa, in November 2022 ended the full-scale war. But it did not settle some of the disputes that had helped fuel it.
One of the deepest disputes concerns western Tigray. Fighters from the neighbouring Amhara region, who fought alongside Ethiopia’s federal army during the 2020-2022 war, took control of western Tigray. Hundreds of thousands of Tigrayans were driven from their homes, and Tigrayan leaders now want the territory returned and those displaced to be allowed to return to their homes.
Many in Amhara reject Tigray’s claim to the territory, however. They argue that western Tigray should not have been incorporated into Tigray when Ethiopia’s regional boundaries were redrawn in 1992, after the fall of the military government.
That dispute is ongoing, even though the TPLF and the Amhara Fano National Movement have now joined the same alliance against Abiy Ahmed’s government.
The federal government also says Tigrayan forces have retained weapons they were meant to surrender. Tigrayan leaders, in turn, say the government has failed to secure the withdrawal of other forces or enable displaced people to return home, particularly to western Tigray.
The political arrangements made after the war have also broken down. The TPLF faction led by Debretsion Gebremichael retook control of Tigray’s administration earlier this year, displacing an interim administration established under the peace agreement.
“Since the end of the war, while the Pretoria Agreement has held, there have been consistent violations on both sides,” Jervin Naidoo, a senior political analyst at Oxford Economics Africa, told Al Jazeera. He said Tigrayans remained aggrieved over western Tigray, the presence of outside forces and the region’s autonomy.
The government sees the TPLF differently. Naidoo said it would portray the group as “a belligerent group trying to destabilise Ethiopia”. But for Tigrayan leaders, he said, renewed fighting could be presented as a matter of protecting their region.
The Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival was announced this month by seven armed movements. Its largest members include the TPLF, the Amhara Fano National Movement and the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA). It also includes groups from Ethiopia’s Somali, Afar and Benishangul-Gumuz areas.
They have different aims and histories, but share a stated objective – to remove Abiy’s government.
Their agreement marks a striking reversal of the alliances formed during the last war, with Fano fighters who fought alongside federal troops against the TPLF now fighting alongside the TPLF.
The Pretoria agreement helped reshape those relationships. It ended the war between Addis Ababa and the TPLF, but Eritrea and Amhara forces, which had supported the government, were not parties to it. Both later fell out with Abiy’s government.
The alliance extends beyond northern Ethiopia. The OLA has fought federal forces in Oromia, in central Ethiopia, since 2018, while a faction of the Ogaden National Liberation Front (ONLF) has joined despite a separate peace agreement signed with the government that year. The ONLF leadership inside Ethiopia’s Somali region says it is not part of the new coalition.
Common opposition to Abiy does not mean the groups agree on Ethiopia’s future. Tigrayan and Amhara members still have competing claims to western Tigray. The government has also accused Eritrea of backing the alliance. Eritrea has repeatedly denied supporting the armed groups.
Small-scale clashes and reported drone strikes preceded this week’s escalation. Fighting then intensified in southern Tigray and spread into the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions.
Each side blames the other for starting the latest major clashes. Tigrayan forces say they responded to a federal offensive involving ground troops and drones. The government side accuses the TPLF of attacking first. With the fighting continuing, claims about individual attacks and territorial gains are difficult to verify independently.
“There has been overnight fighting in the border town of Abala,” Al Jazeera’s Catherine Soi reported from Kenya. The town, located in northern Afar on the border with Tigray, was also affected by the previous war. Reports have differed over who controls the town. On a separate front in Amhara, Ethiopia’s army says it killed more than 270 rebel fighters. That figure has not been independently verified.
Tigrayan forces have taken control of the airports at Mekelle, Axum and Shire, disrupting civilian flights. The African Union says the seizure is inconsistent with the Pretoria agreement. About three-quarters of a million people remained displaced within Tigray because of the earlier war before this latest escalation.
There is a risk it could, but analysts say the conflict has not descended into a full-scale civil war yet. Fighting has crossed Tigray’s borders, and the federal government is already facing armed conflicts in other regions.
There is also a chance of regional escalation. Eritrea fought alongside the Ethiopian government during the previous Tigray war, but relations between the neighbours have since deteriorated, partly over Abiy’s push for access to Red Sea ports. Addis Ababa accuses Eritrea of supporting armed groups inside Ethiopia.
The African Union has called for an immediate halt to the escalation and for renewed talks under the Pretoria agreement. It has asked former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, who helped mediate the 2022 deal, to engage the parties urgently. The East African bloc IGAD has also urged neighbouring countries to avoid actions that could make the crisis worse.

articles.content_orig:

When Alexandru Voica, head of corporate affairs at the video-generation startup Synthesia, sent me a link this summer to the newest addition to their PR team, I was surprised. It was an interactive virtual avatar of him, trained to answer common press questions about Synthesia, like what it does and how it works. The day before, I was on a panel where PR people asked me if I minded pitches that used AI-generated text. But Alexandru’s avatar was beyond that — this seemed to me the final boss of using AI in PR.
In September, Synthesia invited me to its new office space in New York. Originally based in the U.K., Synthesia is a hot digital avatar startup alongside others like D-ID, HeyGen, and Colossyan. It hit a $4 billion valuation earlier this year and said last year it had crossed $100 million in ARR .
Synthesia lets enterprises build interactive training videos with AI avatars and recently launched a product called Roleplay Sessions that lets employees practice, for example, sales pitches with an interactive AI avatar that responds and scores their responses.
When I went to the new office opening and they asked me if I would like my own AI avatar, I didn’t even hesitate to say yes. Of course I would like my own digital twin. My outfit was cute that day, and my hair was in place.
Until I met my digital twin, I had been indifferent toward avatars, but I felt they would inevitably become part of everyday online life. I heard of people on Instagram creating them in their likenesses to help them make social content. I find it all to be very interesting, and it’s perhaps why I have no qualms now presenting to you my digital twin. This is the first time Synethsia has made a digital avatar for a journalist (or for anyone, period, outside of Voica). It is trained on my story about why venture-backed startups commit more fraud than non-VC-backed startups and will only answer questions about that story.
Below, simply press “start in a new window” to begin.
You can ask it questions like:
To make this, I entered a mini film studio nestled inside Synthesia’s office where they took numerous photos of me and captured a two-minute recording of my voice. I had to consent to these avatars being made and, well, digital Dom was born. They created a personal avatar for me (one that just reads whatever script I give it) — with and without glasses — and they made two interactive avatars for me (ones that can talk back and listen to me), also with and without glasses.
We picked an article to train the interactive avatar on, and then one of the teams built my interactive avatar , which is powered by a combination of voice-to-text, video, language, and text-to-voice models. My avatar’s tech stack includes Synthesia’s own video and voice models, although the company also allows customers to choose alternatives from other labs like Cartesia, ElevenLabs, Google, or OpenAI. Enterprises can also choose to host their avatars on whatever cloud they want or pay Synthesia to host them.
The voice-to-text model turns what people say into text, the agentic language model makes sense of text and can take actions based on it, the text-to-voice model turns a response into audio, and finally a video model (built by Synthesia) animates the avatar as it talks.
Overall, Synthesia builds three types of products — a video-creation and distribution platform with classic avatars, where someone types in a script and the avatar repeats it; an agentic platform called Sessions where people can interact with the avatars in surveys or roleplay; and an API platform where people can take Synthesia video and voice models and combine them with other tech services to build interactive avatars or other types of products.
It took the Synthesia team a couple of days to make my avatars. I played first with the personal ones and typed a fairly generic script to see how my AI voice sounded. I had it talk about how fall has arrived in New York, my favorite time of year. The voice was fairly accurate, and I was glad it didn’t pick up any of the hoarseness I had when I recorded my audio sample.
I showed it to some non-tech friends who found it both interesting and creepy.
Then I showed them my interactive one, which is deterministic, meaning it will only say what it was trained to respond to. In this case, that was my venture fraud story. I asked it questions like where I was before TechCrunch and what part of New York I lived in, but each time it directed me back to the story.
My friends didn’t think the voice sounded much like mine and thought the likeness was not as good as the personal avatar, but nonetheless it was close enough to be somewhat creepy. My mom called it “amazing,” which is pretty high praise from her. She and my father kept trying to ask it questions “only they would know” about me — but the model didn’t answer, redirecting them each time to the venture fraud story.
“I don’t remember giving birth to two of you,” she joked after testing the model.
This experience has made me think about what the future of journalism could be. Would people be OK with turning on the news and it being presented by an avatar? One investor told me no immediately. Certainly there is a lot of pushback today on AI slop that has infiltrated social media and other news-sharing platforms. But others I asked weren’t so sure. Could avatars augment — or even replace — journalists? Would CEOs want to talk to an AI avatar of a journalist rather than a human one?
What I like about my career is connecting with people, writing stories, and researching new topics. But the biggest part of journalism is trust. That doesn’t seem like it could ever be outsourced to an AI.
Outside of journalism, I’m confident the idea of cloning yourself could be appealing. No more catching up on work after a holiday or vacation, because a version of you can always be around, answering questions.
We’ll have to see how avatar usage evolves in corporate America. But now that I have my own, I have mixed feelings. After I got over the initial novelty of it, I examined my avatar closely after it stopped talking and waited — for what, I’m not sure. Maybe I’m waiting for it to blink. Or to say something new, or to smile, or to just let me know that it knows.
Because my digital twins are deterministic, they will never do that. But I can see how easy it would be for someone to fall into a tinge of AI psychosis with one that was nondeterministic, meaning powered by a chatbot that was free to pontificate.
I told one investor that, whatever the future of digital twins is, I predict that my generation, Gen Z, likely won’t get used to them. They feel sci-fi: Everything we’ve ever seen in a movie is here now. But I will say, I find digital avatars less jarring than humanoids . At least with an avatar, if stuff gets weird, I can always log off.
Until then, however, here is my personal avatar, giving you a rundown of all the top stories on our site this week!

articles.title_zh: Third suspect arrested in death of Mississippi woman found hanging at ‘staged’ crime scene
articles.content_orig:
A third person has been arrested in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old woman who police said was found hanging from a tree behind an abandoned Mississippi home in August.
Eric Clark, 45, surrendered to police on Friday and is charged with murder. Police also disclosed on Friday that according to an autopsy investigation, “the scene and the hanging were staged.”
No other details were released about the scene or Fortune’s killing.
Clark is expected to appear in court on Monday.
Two other people, Earnest Lloyd Jr. and Jarques Ratliff , were also arrested and charged with murder in connection with her death. Both men are Black.
Police have released very little information about what led up to Fortune’s death. Detectives investigating the case have interviewed as many as 15 people, collected forensic evidence and followed numerous leads, police said in a news release.
Authorities said Ratliff, 51, had an “association” with Fortune but did not release further details.
Lloyd, 25, allegedly had a physical altercation with Fortune either days or minutes before she died, according to NBC affiliate WLBT of Jackson . Police accused Lloyd of hanging Fortune with a black cable cord, WLBT reported.
Ratliff, who pleaded not guilty , and Lloyd were denied bond at separate court hearings.

The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Saturday (September 26, 2026) announced a slew of measures addressing concerns over the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls across the country, including stopping physical hearings for unmapped voters or those with logical discrepancies in their enumeration forms.
It said that the declaration accompanying Form 6 (used for fresh voter registration) is mandatory only during the current SIR process. This in effect means that new voters who seek inclusion in electoral rolls after the ongoing SIR need not submit any such declaration.
The commission also said that any person whose name has got left out during SIR or thereafter, and any person including young/ first-time voters, may apply to the electoral registration officer (ERO) concerned, for inclusion of their names in the electoral rolls.  A special drive will immediately be launched for their enrolment, it said in a press note.
The SIR process has already been completed in 20 States and Union Territories.
The fresh initiatives of the poll body came after a meeting of the full bench of the commission on Saturday afternoon (September 26, 2026) and days after reports emerged of a rift within the Election Commissioners over these and other issues in the SIR process as well as the internal working of the ECI.
The press note confirmed that the two Commissioners had written to the Cabinet Secretary but said it was not related to any policy matter of the commission or IT division but related to working of an officer on deputation to the ECI. “The work re-distribution orders issued by the concerned officer were not actually implemented after the orders of the two Commissioners,” it clarified.
The commission’s press note was pertinently accompanied by a photograph of all the three Election Commissioners and mentioned that it “has the approval of the full commission”.
As far as physical hearings were concerned, the statement said: “In case of any person to whom notice has been issued during the ongoing SIR, for being unmapped and for logical discrepancies, BLOs (booth-level officers) will visit the homes of such persons for collection of documents and thereafter upload them on the ECINet, for decision by the ERO.”
“Such persons need not be called for hearing to ERO/AERO office. Only in exceptional circumstances, as decided by the ERO, the hearing will be held preferably online. Any adult member of the family can be authorised by the elector to attend the hearing on their behalf, if required. Facilities for the online hearing are to be strengthened.”
As regards new voter registration, the EC maintained that the declaration form attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Supreme Court, but for non-SIR period, the forms appFmahalicable as per rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used for new voter inclusion.
Also read | Declaration part of Form 6 changed since SIR in Bihar
The other issue that had attracted the ire of the two Election Commissioners was the supposed centralisation of management of voter rolls through the ECINet portal, with field officers unable to access it in many cases.
The statement said that “A Committee headed by Sr. Deputy Election Commissioner (DEC) and including an independent expert from IIT/IIIT will review the ECINET to double-check that it complies with the provisions of the Acts and Rules and submit report to the Commission”. It added that henceforth, all the new initiatives about IT modules and portals will be discussed in the Committee of Officers (COO) before approval by the commission.
“Field officers have role-based access to the ECINET system as per their statutory powers. In case, any further flexibility is required by the field officers, that will be made operational,” it added.
The commission also extended the period for filing claims and objections for Delhi till October 30 and for Maharashtra till October 12.
Many other administrative measures were also announced. These include circulation of an advanced agenda and issuance of minutes for all of Commission’s meetings, completion of annual performance appraisal reports of all the officers within the stipulated time frame, approval of the commission for foreign trips of officers and compliance with all directions issued by the Commissioners to the officers of the Commission.
The Opposition, which has been seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, remained unimpressed with the statement. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said: “The CEC thinks he can hide behind protocol. He stands exposed and is now petrified as an entire country seeks to hold him accountable.”
“The ongoing SIR which has turned to be method of massive disenfranchisement of several crores of India must be suspended immediately without delay. In the meantime, nothing short of the CEC’s resignation or prosecution will suffice”.
